sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Pajson is a real cashew processor expanding from 18,000 to 53,000 MTPA, not merely a listed growth story. Comparable revenue has grown 36.24% annually from FY23 to FY26, and operating EBITDA reached 36.63 cr. The hard question is whether a larger plant converts those sales into cash and per-share value. Cumulative FY23–26 CFO is only 12.38% of PAT, supplier advances are substantial, and most headline cash is reserved IPO money rather than working-capital liquidity.
BQS is 5.2, GQS raw 6.5 is capped at 5.0 for persistent weak cash realization, and IAS is NS because ordinary funded expected return remains unestablished. All four gates are Conditional, not evidenced governance failure or present insolvency. The documented 20 cr project term sanction and WC facilities are material positive evidence: a 3 cr conditional cash-headroom test closes the base timing gap. But sanctions are not receipts and project money cannot bridge unrestricted working capital.
At 328 INR, market capitalization is 780.95 cr and current-share P/E 31.51x. A separately hypothetical, fully prefunded base case yields 9.62%, below the 15% five-year hurdle; bear-21.98%, bull 24.81%. These are conditional analytical outcomes, not target returns or a recommendation to transact.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Issuer: Pajson Agro India Limited, BSE SME 544657, ISIN INE14LM01012. Information cutoff 20 October 2026; market reference 19 October 2026; research retrieval 22 October 2026. Scope is standalone because no operating subsidiaries are reported. All financial amounts are INR crore unless stated otherwise. The five-year equity horizon is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, ACT/365.25, with a 15% nominal pre-tax hurdle. The 500,000 INR position is illustrative and not a claim about the reader's portfolio.
Primary coverage includes full FY23–FY26 annual reports and actual audit annexures, IPO restatements, March and June monitoring reports, bank disclosures, rating rationale, investor call/presentation, latest capital reconciliation and voluntary Q1 business update. FY22 is a short inception period, not a comparable fifth full year. The latest Q1 sales estimate supplies a revenue-only update, not an audited earnings or cash-flow TTM.
Market evidence is narrower: 60 exact dated secondary OHLC/volume rows match the official trading calendar; 19 have actual turnover and 41 use low×volume conservative bounds. Missing NSE issuer rows are expected for a BSE-only stock and are not zero-volume days. The current official master verifies 600 lot and dated price-band fields, but its SM/ST eligibility flags are not decoded as ASM/GSM clearance. Live spread, depth, current exchange surveillance and free float beyond reported ownership are not authenticated.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
All 13 primitive factors are scored once on the v 3.0 scale, with two material facts, contrary evidence, confidence and score-change tests retained below. Unknown expected return is NS, not 0. BQS uses governance 20%, moat 20%, revenue 12%, durability 10%, incremental capital 12%, cash 10%, balance 8% and execution 8%. GQS uses revenue 40%, durability 20%, earnings 15%, capital 15% and cash 10%. IAS uses final unrounded BQS 25%, expected return 35%, downside 20%, price 10% and liquidity 10%.
REV begins at 9 because the selected comparable revenue CAGR exceeds 30%, but Medium confidence and short history cap it at 8. No extra trajectory point is awarded for a single estimated quarter. Commodity volume and material-contribution cross-checks support operating expansion, while incomplete price/yield/mix attribution limits confidence. This is not an acquisition-driven series after the initial plant purchase. CAP is 6 rather than a premium score because strong accounting incremental returns partly reflect recovery and do not validate the uncommissioned plant cohort.
BQS and capped GQS are complete and may be compared with their conditions visible. IAS has 65% coverage; its mathematical range is not a ranking score or probability interval. Persistent CASH 3 triggers the GQS ceiling 5 after calculation. R remains NS until unrestricted funding is demonstrated; a fully funded hypothetical recapitalization cannot supply an ordinary expected-return score. Q is the exact final BQS, not its one-decimal display.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company procures raw cashew nuts, processes and grades kernels, sells to institutions and distributors, and is developing Royal Mewa consumer products. Husk and shells provide by-product receipts; traded dry fruit is a smaller activity. FY26 kernel revenue 239.2421 cr represents about 93.56% of operating revenue, so cashew economics dominate. Production involves sourcing, steaming, shelling, drying, peeling, grading and packing. Yield, whole-versus-broken mix, procurement season and customer realization matter more than a headline industry TAM.
The original Rolugunta plant was acquired from Olam in December 2021. The May presentation also refers to 55,000 MTPA and a 20% brand ambition, whereas current plant arithmetic is 18,000+35,000=53,000 MTPA and the call discusses 15% brand revenue. The model uses the lower 53,000 physical ceiling and does not treat aspirational brand percentages as earned sales. The current 18,000 MTPA footprint and a 35,000 MTPA Vizianagaram project create a plausible step-up in capacity. The project's 74.88 cr budget, machinery purchases and development costs are investments, not customer orders. Sales-equivalent modeled volumes start from 18,000×86%=15,480 MT, explicitly an approximation rather than audited production. Procurement 15,726 MT is a different measure and is not relabeled processing output.
Imported raw materials create FX, freight, crop and geographic supply exposure. Different management disclosures give different import proportions and sourcing periods; these are not spliced into one precise full-year percentage. Financial FX outgo and related-supplier concentration are more solid accounting anchors. Institutional share 33.96%, a broad distributor network and a small brand provide several selling channels, but none guarantees off-take for the new plant.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Processing competence, sourcing relationships, grading consistency, by-product monetization and institutional qualification are useful capabilities. Management cites 24.57% yield and a roughly 70: 30 whole/broken mix; such operating indicators can protect contribution if repeatedly delivered. However, units and definitions differ between IPO KPIs and later calls. RCN-equivalent realization must not be confused with kernel selling price, and a single good yield is not proof of a durable low-cost moat.
Entry requires equipment, working capital and supply/customer relationships, but these are obtainable by competing processors. RHP peers such as Krishival, Prospect and Aelea illustrate a competitive processing/distribution landscape; different products and channels prevent a mechanical peer-multiple valuation. Royal Mewa's reported 6.5x growth is from a small base. The ambition to reach 15% of sales over 3–5 years is not an observed premium brand franchise.
The economic cross-check is mixed: the material-contribution proxy grew 33.33% in FY26, close to sales growth 36.55%, while the proxy margin slipped from 27.03% to 26.39%. This supports genuine value-added expansion, but not widening structural pricing power. Manufacturing wages and overheads are not allocated in that proxy, so it must not be called audited gross profit. MOAT 5 reflects useful but contestable capabilities, not a compounder premium.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue rose from 101.1188 cr in FY23 to 255.7221 cr in FY26, a 36.24% three-year CAGR and 154.6033 cr absolute addition, averaging 51.5344 cr annually. The path is uneven: FY24 declined to 95.9121 cr, FY25 recovered to 187.2683 cr and FY26 increased 36.55%. The FY24–26 CAGR 63.29% starts from a weak year and is shown, not chosen to maximize the score. FY22 revenue 15.4642 cr is a short inception period with a purchased plant and is not a clean five-year base.
RHP processed-volume observations rise from 7,298.88 MT in FY23 to 10,416.94 MT in FY25, about 19.47% annually, versus 36.09% sales CAGR in the same window. Thus realization, yields and product mix also matter. Table labels and later management RCN-equivalent KPIs differ, preventing a fully precise volume/price decomposition. FY26 material-contribution growth and physical capacity utilization provide corroboration, not an invented audited production series.
The July 28 voluntary update estimates Q1 FY27 sales 67.94 cr versus 45.03 cr, growth 50.88%. Replacing prior Q1 in FY26 yields revenue-only TTM 278.6321 cr. There is no matching audited quarterly PAT, cash-flow or balance-sheet update, so no earnings TTM or automatic REV upgrade follows. Growth quality hinges on sell-through, realization and collections rather than simply filling installed machines.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The capacity project is real and potentially meaningful, but accessible demand and finance must arrive together. June monitoring reports 9.40 cr cumulative IPO project use and 47.60 cr remaining project principal, plus 0.09 cr residual GCP. Management targets trial production in Q3 FY27. CTE and irrigation permissions were obtained in March, while other approvals and execution milestones were still pending at the June review. Construction delays attributed to labor/festival and land leveling are disclosed rather than ignored.
The original 57 cr IPO/17.88 cr internal-accrual project plan was revised to use a 20 cr institutional term loan, with July 16 shareholder approval described by the monitor. Kotak's actual sanction is stronger evidence than a merely proposed finance plan. The 20 cr/84 month term is modeled only against eligible contemporaneous project costs, after restricted IPO cash is consumed; it is not free WC liquidity. The 7.50 cr 90 day WCDL/LC enhancement and HSBC 30 cr including 20 cr LC are separate facility facts. Neither rating 75 cr nor total sanctioned limits is added as a cash receipt.
The remaining project cash budget is 64.41 cr after 10.47 cr already paid as advances against issued purchase orders in management's May bridge; acquired land is excluded from the stated project cost. An old 0.2972 cr capital-creditor obligation is paid once within old current claims; new modeled project payments are 64.1128 cr. The 45 cr machinery PO is not a second added project cost. Capital-return estimates compare incremental normalized NOPAT and invested capital, not current ROCE. A 26.43% historical proxy exceeds a reasoned 13–16% funding-risk benchmark, but new capacity has yet to prove its own cash return. CASH 3 therefore caps GQS at 5 despite the growth opportunity.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
March promoter ownership is 62.47%; ownership concentration itself is not misconduct. The important stewardship questions are related sourcing, supplier advances and use-of-proceeds discipline. Related raw purchases fell from 111.0576 cr in FY25 to 36.9269 cr in FY26, a favorable diversification signal. Yet P Global DMCC advance rose from 3.2816 cr to 14.0775 cr. The IPO history of heavy related sourcing and absent long-term customer commitments warrants arm-length and settlement evidence, not an allegation of tunneling.
Both monitoring reports describe expense savings transferred to GCP, raising its allocation to 10.43 cr against a 10 cr limit without corresponding approval on record. Board approval of the transfer is not automatically the required approval for exceeding the limit. The issue is bounded, disclosed and important for minority treatment; it is not evidence that all IPO cash is missing. June project/GCP/expense buckets reconcile to 26.76 cr cumulative use and 47.69 cr unused principal. Actual receipts and interest are separated from object allocations.
FY26 auditor resignation was explained by the engagement partner surrendering the practice certificate, expressly without other concerns. A subsequent auditor appointment is documented; no negative inference is made merely from the change. Execution is mixed: existing capacity, institutional penetration and machinery ordering are positives, while permits, construction timing and the large new-plant ramp remain unresolved milestones. A short listing record prevents a high-confidence long-cycle stewardship score.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The full FY26 main opinion and actual IFC annexure are unmodified; no reported fraud, loan default or going-concern material uncertainty was found. CARO still reports old statutory PF/ESIC dues, quarterly stock/book-debt statement differences and incomplete database-level audit-trail information. Total contractor dues in Note 9 are not the same subset as CARO amounts overdue more than six months. June bank difference 29.09 lakhs and smaller later differences are retained. December's 6552.47−6550.93 equals 1.54 lakhs, not the printed 1.95. These bounded issues do not justify declaring the whole financial series unusable.
Historical originals add context. FY24 PDF 12 says the audit trail was enabled only in the second half of the year, with no tampering found after enablement. The actual IFC Annexure B exists at PDF 18–19, but its clean-text opinion says effective 31 March 2023 despite a 30 August 2024 signature, an apparent carry-forward-date inconsistency. FY25 PDF 20–32 contains unmodified main and actual IFC opinions, while PDF 24 already discloses the third-party database-trail limitation repeated in FY26. PDF 25–27 record a June 2024 bank-stock discrepancy attributed to clerical error and older PF/ESIC/APMC arrears; PDF 29 explicitly records predecessor resignation without issues, objections or concerns. Later current-year clean reporting does not retroactively fill missing earlier logs. These bounded historical exceptions reinforce G2 Conditional, not an unsupported fraud finding or automatic reliability Hold.
Several presentation bridges need care. FY26 PAT 2478.38 lakhs and the labeled weighted-share count 23,809,595 do not produce EPS 12.82; full-current-share EPS 10.40916 is used for valuation, while likely IPO weighting is not invented as a corrected audited figure. Capital-note IPO expenses 702.97 lakhs differ from reserve deductions 650.90+90.55=741.45 lakhs. Cash net 6703.88 lakhs reconciles to gross 7445.33 less 741.45, so the difference is not treated as unspent cash. The CF line labeled cash generated from operations is actually a WC subtotal: 3723.23−4305.62−808.94=−1391.33 lakhs final CFO.
Original FY23 PAT−73.26 lakhs became restated+1.67; original FY24 PAT 410.37 became 335.31; FY25 variants are also retained. Disclosed timing, stores/benefit and tax adjustments explain why sources must not be mixed opportunistically. Latest annual FY25 CFO 1724.07 lakhs differs from RHP 1612.78, with corresponding capex variants. Both bases lead to weak cumulative cash realization. Annual rows retain original/restated labels, null unavailable gross profit and unrestricted-cash fields, reported versus current-share EPS and the full normalization formula.
Refined FY26 operating capital 117.9372 cr is fixed assets 52.1191 plus ONWC 65.8181. Equity plus debt minus all cash gives 115.1762. The 2.7610 residual reconciles through DTL 1.4876, all provisions 0.8229, excluded nonoperating current claims 0.9268, less tax/interest receivables 0.4762 and 0.0001 rounding. Old current claims 0.9654 include 0.0386 of provisions; remaining 0.7843 is deducted once at terminal. Project deposits and land already embedded in operating value are not separately added to equity. No unexplained balancing plug is used.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The 328 INR reference quote and 23,809,595 current shares imply 780.954716 cr market value. FY26 current-share EPS is 10.40916 and P/E 31.51x. Removing other income and using 25% tax gives normalized PAT 23.992425 cr. A mixed-date EV diagnostic adds March gross debt 34.2425 and deducts only modeled immediately free cash 2.5522, giving 812.645016 cr, or 22.19x operating EBITDA 36.6284. Deducting all 55.099 cr cash would incorrectly treat earmarked project balances as distributable. These are March-balance/October-price diagnostics, not certified October net debt.
The dated model starts 31 March 2026 to test pre-entry funding, and stops 19 October 2031. It separates restricted IPO cash, later FD maturities, old current claims, related debt due 20 March 2027, three-month WCDL repayment/redraw and project-only term draws. Interest rates, draw eligibility, CC continuation and renewal are assumptions where actual contracts are incomplete. Term amortization starts one year after assumed facility availability rather than authenticated first draw; that earlier repayment convention is conservative. Extra WCDL tests assume cash eligibility and are not claims that the 7.5 cr mixed limit is automatically fund-based. Every interval tests an opening/post-event balance, a conservative pre-positive-operating-receipt trough and an ending balance. Maintenance, positive incremental ONWC, project cash, interest and tax cannot be paid with later same-interval revenue. A 2 cr reserve approximates four weeks of payroll/other operating costs; 0/1/2/3/5 cr sensitivities avoid mistaking that choice for a statutory solvency requirement.
The no-extra-WC base gap is 1.69 cr and first breaches on 1 April 2026; ordinary and non-rescue return/entry-price fields are null. An explicitly conditional 3 cr extra WCDL test closes the base path, but 30–34% ONWC/sales still causes gaps. Strict no-roll cases are adverse financing scenarios, not evidence of an actual default. The hypothetical prefunding illustration issues whole shares immediately after the 31 March balance timestamp at 119.36 INR, a 20% discount to the dated 149.20 INR reference, with 5% fees. Base net 1.69 cr and ownership dilution 0.62% lead to 9.62%; neither issue terms nor historical receipt actually occurred.
Base assumptions are 18% volume growth, 2% realization growth, 14% EBITDA margin, 26% ONWC/sales, 2% maintenance capex and 12x exit. Terminal sales-equivalent utilization is 73.22% of 53,000 MTPA. At this fixed physical path, the fully funded reverse solver requires EBITDA margins 15.35%/17.23%/19.31% for 12%/15%/18% returns. Each candidate resizes funding and shares, retains its finite bracket and residual, and does not assume a free rescue. Multiple/growth/WC/capex/delay/debt and cash-allocation sensitivities are embedded completely.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is a cash mismatch, not a claim that cashew demand disappears. Imported raw-cost/FX/freight pressure compresses processing spreads while inventory and supplier advances tie up cash. The new plant needs capital before it earns revenue; delayed permissions and a slower ramp can coincide with short WCDL maturities and the March 2027 related-loan settlement. Customer concentration can make a volume miss disproportionately painful.
The bear model combines 6% volume growth, 1% realization growth, 9% EBITDA margin, 34% ONWC/sales, 20% project overrun, delayed commissioning and 8x exit. Even after hypothetical full prefunding it materially destroys common-equity value. The base at 30% rather than 26% working-capital intensity has a much larger need; extra 7.5 cr conditional WC does not close every stress. The 20 cr LC component of HSBC is never counted as cash. Unused project term sanctions are never unrestricted receipts.
Hard assets and book equity are counterevidence to a zero-value narrative, but no independent plant/inventory liquidation appraisal supports a price floor. Advances may settle as materials rather than cash, collateral limits recovery flexibility, and a new equity issue dilutes existing owners. Modeled reserve breaches are not assertions of observed default or fraud. Cash at zero, reserve shortfall and lack of verified headroom are different conditions, and the sensitivity rows distinguish them.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A 5x or 10x outcome must fit physical output, contribution, funding and share count. At 12x terminal EBITDA and 14% margin, with zero net claims and no dilution, 5x current equity value requires revenue 2324.27 cr and sales-equivalent throughput about 126,049 MT at the base terminal realization.10x requires 4648.54 cr and 252,097 MT. Both materially exceed the planned 53,000 MTPA capacity. These are simple scale diagnostics, not universal lower bounds: accumulated cash could help, while debt, claims and dilution make the requirement harder.
Therefore a multibagger path would need further financed plants, substantially higher value per tonne/margins, a much longer horizon, a much lower entry price or a higher terminal multiple. None is silently granted. Brand success could change realization and economics, but the current small base and stated ambition do not validate that transformation. A larger market alone cannot deliver a 5x equity outcome. The existing capacity plan can support meaningful revenue growth without supporting extravagant return claims at this quote.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain the latest bank cash, FD restrictions/maturities, facility utilization and eligible undrawn cash limits; distinguish sanction, draw, LC and renewal.
2. Verify 20 cr term eligibility, cost reimbursement rules, actual draw schedule/rate and 84 month amortization; project finance must remain project finance.
3. Resolve the monitor's GCP cap-approval exception and reconcile March/June principal, accrued interest and object use without double counting.
4. Track pending permits, revised commissioning dates, total cost-to-complete and actual trial/commercial output; a PO is not completed production.
5. Require audited sales, PAT, CFO and balance-sheet updates. Separate volume, yield, realization and institutional/brand mix.
6. Follow inventory days, supplier advances, related-party settlements, receivable aging and cumulative CFO/PAT. Weak cash despite sales is a falsification signal.
7. Verify March 2027 related principal/interest settlement and three-month bank renewals before treating funding as resilient.
8. Obtain corrected weighted-share/EPS, IPO-expense and bank-return arithmetic bridges, statutory-dues closure and database audit-trail evidence.
9. Recalculate incremental returns after new plant output begins, rather than crediting pre-commissioning earnings to that plant.
10. Before implementation, verify 600 lot, BSE surveillance/price restrictions, executable spread/depth and whole-lot participation for the actual position. This is a research checklist, not an activated monitoring service.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Insufficient evidence for a complete current investment-attractiveness assessment; mixed-quality expansion watchlist. The business has real operating scale and a plausible growth project, but no evidence-backed compounder designation. BQS 5.18 and capped GQS 5.0 describe the business with their conditions visible; IAS remains NS, so the numeric classification matrix cannot supply an investment rank.
A lower share price alone would not repair unverified funding. Conversely, the documented sanctions and modest base timing gap mean it would be excessive to declare funding failure merely because daily treasury balances are unavailable. G3 remains Conditional, with explicit cash-headroom tests showing a plausible resolution route. If eligible cash availability and maturity coverage are verified, the ordinary model can be completed and scored; it must still clear the 15% hurdle and downside/lot constraints.
The conditions for a stronger thesis are timely commercial production, acceptable new-cohort incremental cash returns, sustained conversion of earnings into cash, related advance discipline, clean use-of-proceeds follow-through and a price that does not require optimistic margins. Until then, hypothetical rescued returns are explanatory sensitivities, not an actionable financing plan or purchase recommendation.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source coverage includes full annual reports, audit annexures, IPO restated accounts, monitoring reports, bank disclosures and dated operating updates from the company, rating agency and exchange. Original versus restated financial figures and management estimates are distinguished. Market prices and turnover remain qualified secondary evidence where exchange-history rows were unavailable. Complete financial and scenario tables accompany the analysis, but accounting normalization cannot eliminate commercial uncertainty.
Unresolved questions are the exact current free-cash/restricted-FD bridge, actual incremental eligible bank headroom and renewal, project draw and amortization terms, GCP approval exception, related advance settlement, weighted-share/EPS and IPO-expense differences, and current execution restrictions. These are bounded uncertainties, not a claim that the business or accounts are fictitious. The full FY26 IFC annexure was inspected; its existence is not an open question.
Analyst assumptions include a 25% normalized tax rate, future growth/margin/WC/capex paths, 2 cr reserve with explicit alternatives, FD maturity availability, inferred bank draw split, conditional rollover, term interest/amortization, conservative within-interval payment order, hypothetical rescue price/fees and terminal multiples. No dividends, terminal IPO-cash distribution, unused sanction cash or automatic LC monetization are assumed. The model's sales-equivalent volume and price are a capacity discipline, not audited physical production or quoted kernel prices. Contrary evidence and confidence are stated throughout; a published disclosure is not an independent guarantee of commercial outcomes.

evidence.claim: Pajson Agro India Limited is BSE 544657, ISIN INE14LM01012. September capital reconciliation confirms 23,809,595 shares; the 19 October official security master gives a 600-share lot.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Security-master SM/ST flags are not a decoded live surveillance clearance.

evidence.claim: FY26 revenue 255.7221 cr, PAT 24.7838 cr and operating EBITDA excluding other income 36.6284 cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: The reported weighted-share label and EPS do not reconcile; current-share EPS is independently computed, not copied.

evidence.claim: Comparable FY23–FY26 revenue CAGR 36.2423%; FY24 revenue declined before recovery and capacity expansion.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: No five-year comparable full-year history; FY22 is an inception/plant-acquisition period. Price, yield and mix are not completely separated.

evidence.claim: Existing 18,000 MTPA and proposed 35,000 MTPA plant imply 53,000 MTPA total; management says existing utilization about 86%.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: New capacity was not commissioned at the audited date; management targets are not actual production.

evidence.claim: Original Olam plant acquired December 2021; no later acquisition in the comparable revenue series.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Organic expansion includes purchased original assets and commodity realization changes; it is not same-store demand alone.

evidence.claim: FY25 top 10 customers 59.63%, largest 19.89%; H1 FY26 top 10 about 60.10%.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Institutional share and distribution access are increasing, but disclosed contracts do not guarantee long-term volume.

evidence.claim: FY26 institutional sales 33.96% versus 20.88% FY25; Royal Mewa growth is from a small base.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Brand aspiration of 15% revenue in 3–5 years and 6.5x growth do not establish consumer pricing power.

evidence.claim: FY23–FY26 cumulative CFO 6.0134 cr versus PAT 48.5602 cr; cash capex 27.8607 cr and additional capital advances 10.623 cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: FY25 CFO 17.2407 cr is positive contrary evidence; the older RHP FY25 CFO 16.1278 cr is retained separately.

evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: The printed intermediate cash-flow subtotal is misleadingly labeled but the full arithmetic reconciles.

evidence.claim: Refined operating capital 117.9372 cr comprises 52.1191 cr fixed operating assets and 65.8181 cr ONWC; broad FY23–26 incremental NOPAT/capital proxy 26.43%.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: This is not the new plant IRR; utilization and margin recovery contribute, and capital advances have not earned operating profit yet.

evidence.claim: March reported cash 55.099 cr includes earmarked IPO deposits; modeled immediately free cash 2.5522 cr after conservative maturity separation.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: CARO labels 52.4451 cr idle IPO FDs. A stricter allocation and 0/1/2/3/5 cr reserve sensitivity are retained; 2.5522 is an analyst bridge, not bank-certified free cash.

evidence.claim: June monitoring shows project spend 9.40 cr, GCP 10.34 cr, expenses 7.02 cr; unused 47.69 cr is 47.60 project plus 0.09 GCP.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Earned FD interest is separately restricted in the model. The June balance is not added to March cash.

evidence.claim: Both March and June monitors note revised GCP allocation 10.43 cr exceeds the 10 cr limit without corresponding approval on record.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: December board approval for transferring expense savings does not itself establish approval for exceeding that limit; this is a procedural concern, not fraud evidence.

evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Facility sanction is real financing-access evidence, but cash draw dates, rates, covenants, utilization and incremental headroom are not fully authenticated.

evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: LC is not cash. Residual 10 cr is modeled only as conditional cash capacity, with assumed interest and repayment, not verified availability.

evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: The share-capital note says IPO expenses 702.97 lakhs; these variants are preserved, not silently merged or treated as spare cash.

summary:
Pajson is a real cashew processor expanding from 18,000 to 53,000 MTPA, not merely a listed growth story. Comparable revenue has grown 36.24% annually from FY23 to FY26, and operating EBITDA reached 36.63 cr. The hard question is whether a larger plant converts those sales into cash and per-share value. Cumulative FY23–26 CFO is only 12.38% of PAT, supplier advances are substantial, and most headline cash is reserved IPO money rather than working-capital liquidity.
BQS is 5.2, GQS raw 6.5 is capped at 5.0 for persistent weak cash realization, and IAS is NS because ordinary funded expected return remains unestablished. All four gates are Conditional, not evidenced governance failure or present insolvency. The documented 20 cr project term sanction and WC facilities are material positive evidence: a 3 cr conditional cash-headroom test closes the base timing gap. But sanctions are not receipts and project money cannot bridge unrestricted working capital.
At 328 INR, market capitalization is 780.95 cr and current-share P/E 31.51x. A separately hypothetical, fully prefunded base case yields 9.62%, below the 15% five-year hurdle; bear-21.98%, bull 24.81%. These are conditional analytical outcomes, not target returns or a recommendation to transact.
